paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God comes back to live with His people. The glory of the LORD enters the temple through the gate facing east, and Ezekiel hears Him say, "this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever." (Ezekiel 43:4, 7) Forever, baker! Not for a season, not until somebody messes it up again.

But look at how He wants to be close. He says Israel defiled His holy name, and then He says, "Now let them remove far from Me their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings, and I will dwell among them forever." (Ezekiel 43:8-9) He tells Ezekiel to describe the temple so the people may be ashamed of their iniquities. God doesn't hide the sin and He doesn't pretend it away, so you don't have to either, friend.

And the altar shows us the way in. Before anything else happens there, it gets seven days of sin offerings and atonement, and then the Lord GOD says, "Then I will accept you." (Ezekiel 43:26-27) I think that's the part to carry out of the bakery today: God makes the way for people to come near, and He is the One who does the accepting. This vision is NOT done yet, so keep your apron on.
